verdicts.author: loop
verdicts.why: No forward promise pulling to the next line. 'She's the trophy, and nobody asked her twice' is the narrator's opinion/aside about the moment, which is judgment, not a loop.

verdicts.author: reasoning
verdicts.why: No character's thinking or WHY is given. 'Every time he loses, an adult relocates him' states a recurring consequence/cost that befalls him, which is stake, not reasoning.

verdicts.author: loop
verdicts.why: 'Tonight he's running again' is a reflective callback commenting on the meaning of the moment; it does not promise or pull toward the next line. That is judgment, not a loop.

hook.why: The hook sells the premise as a trailer voice: a boy who only crashes dropped into a city built on control. The question is film-level (will he survive), stays unanswered through line 15, uses only generic world properties (cars drive sideways, owes a stranger a car, hasn't learned to turn) with no specific frame, and pays off the title's shipped-to-Tokyo/owing-a-car premise.

title.why: States an extraordinary premise as plain fact (shipped to Tokyo to dodge jail, ends up owing the yakuza a car) and withholds the outcome with 'He Cannot Pay For'. It frames the setup without revealing the ending.
